summary.headline: The School Committee reviewed a preliminary 5.36% FY28 budget increase, evaluated Neary building designs, and confirmed the Neary roof project finished under budget.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee reviewed the preliminary FY28 budget proposal, which projects a 5.36% level-service increase driven by salaries, special education tuitions, transportation, and utilities. Tappe Architects presented updated schematic designs for the proposed Neary Elementary School addition and renovation, prompting committee debate over whether to partner with the MSBA or pursue local funding. District officials also reported that the Neary roof replacement is over 97% complete and well under its $4.5 million appropriation, and the committee approved FY27 federal and state grants.

topics.title: School principals report
topics.summary: Principals presented building updates across the district. Highlights included outdoor planting and student council activities at Finn, a successful $27,000 SOS color run fundraiser and fire safety visits at Woodward, math curriculum milestones and student values awards at Neary, and middle school field trips to Boundless Adventures and Washington, D.C. for Trottier students.
key_details: Woodward Memorial School raised $27,000 through its fall SOS color run, exceeding its $20,000 target.
Trottier eighth graders returned from an educational field trip to Washington, D.C., which included tours of the Holocaust Museum and the Capitol.
Finn Elementary launched a student council with representatives from pre-K and first-grade classrooms.

topics.title: Trottier Middle School improvement plan
topics.summary: Trottier leadership presented their annual action plan under Vision 2026, outlining strategic initiatives for learning, curriculum, and school climate. The school implemented a new six-day rotating schedule featuring dedicated intervention and reading blocks, while continuing curriculum rollouts in Carnegie Math and Amplify Science.
key_details: Current Trottier enrollment is 419 students, including 81 on IEPs and 46 on 504 plans.
The newly launched six-day rotating schedule includes Drop Everything and Read (DEAR) and FLEX intervention periods.
Staff are developing common assessments in mathematics in collaboration with Melican Middle School in Northborough.

topics.title: Whitsons food service evaluation criteria
topics.summary: Administration outlined the evaluation criteria tool for food service vendor Whitsons Culinary Group during the first quarter of their contract. District administration will perform the evaluation and deliver a data-driven report and recommendation to the School Committee in December.
key_details: The food service contract is an annual contract requiring committee review.
Committee members were invited to visit school cafeterias to sample lunches prior to the December evaluation.
The administration will compile evaluation data from all district schools.
topics.outcome: District administration will present evaluation findings and recommendations at the December meeting.

topics.title: Capital and roof project updates
topics.summary: Administrators updated the committee on active school capital projects, focusing on roof replacements and floor investigations. The Neary roof project is more than 97% complete and is projected to cost roughly $2.91 million, coming in almost $1.6 million under the $4.5 million town meeting appropriation. Design work for the Trottier roof will be submitted to the MSBA for 60% construction design review ahead of public bidding.
key_details: Neary roof replacement is over 97% complete, with final costs projected around $2,909,143 against a $4.5 million appropriation.
Unused borrowing authorization from the Neary project will reduce the town's overall debt service impact.
Trottier roof replacement will submit 60% construction designs to the MSBA soon, aiming to bid in December or early January.
Architects from DRA are analyzing moisture levels in Finn Elementary floors to finalize repair specifications for summer 2027 work.
topics.outcome: Projects remain on schedule with Neary roof entering punch-list completion.
topics.why_it_matters: The Neary roof coming in $1.6 million under budget reduces borrowing costs for Southborough taxpayers, while upcoming bids on the Trottier roof will set major capital spending for next summer.

topics.title: Neary school building committee design update and MSBA discussion
topics.summary: Tappe Architects presented refined schematic designs for Option 3, an addition and renovation plan for Neary Elementary School. The plan includes a new secure front entry, expanding the gymnasium into the interior courtyard to create a full-size facility, infilling wide hallways for breakout learning, and removing all modular classrooms. The committee also debated whether to submit a Statement of Interest to the MSBA core building program in January 2027 or proceed with a town-funded project, weighing state reimbursement against a 4-to-5-year delay and rising construction inflation.
key_details: Option 3 adds a secure front entrance, relocates central administration out of the building, and eliminates all modular units.
The proposed gymnasium infill expands into the existing courtyard, creating two full teaching stations and elevated clearance for sports.
Special education and student support spaces will be integrated into fourth- and fifth-grade classroom clusters rather than isolated.
The superintendent presented a financial model showing an MSBA core project could push completion to 2035 or later, with inflation potentially eroding state reimbursement benefits.
A joint meeting with the Select Board and other boards will be scheduled to seek townwide consensus on whether to submit an MSBA application.
topics.outcome: The Elementary School Building Committee will review detailed cost estimates on November 12, followed by joint discussions with the Select Board.
topics.why_it_matters: Deciding between partnering with the MSBA or financing the school renovation locally will determine whether Southborough waits nearly a decade for project completion and how much local taxpayers will ultimately pay.

topics.title: Superintendent enrollment and financial report
topics.summary: The superintendent reported steady enrollment based on October 1 data and NESDEC projections. Business officials reviewed the October monthly financial report, noting a remaining budget balance of $332,720 (1.27% of the budget), and presented $747,857 in entitlement and special education grants.
key_details: Pre-K through grade 8 enrollment remains stable and aligns with long-term demographic forecasts.
General fund budget balance as of October 31 stood at $332,720, down about $17,000 from the prior month.
Four districtwide administration function codes remain overexpended due to reallocating shared personnel salaries, which will be rebalanced in FY28.
The district received $747,857 in FY27 federal and state grants, a slight decrease of $86,000 primarily due to lower IDEA allocations.
topics.outcome: The committee voted to accept the October general fund report, approve overexpended function codes, and accept FY27 grant awards.

topics.title: FY28 capital plan review
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the draft FY28 capital plan totaling $710,000 in proposed warrant articles, excluding the Neary project placeholder. Proposed work includes replacing sinks at Trottier and Finn, installing safety fencing at Finn along Parkerville Road, and replacing front exterior stairs at Woodward.
key_details: Proposed FY28 capital requests total $710,000, including projects eligible for MSBA accelerated repair consideration.
Finn fencing project options were developed in collaboration with the Department of Public Works to prevent vehicle incursions.
A $45 million placeholder remains listed for the Neary renovation project pending final scope and timeline decisions.
topics.outcome: The Capital Planning Committee will meet November 16 to review the requests.

topics.title: Preliminary FY28 operating budget presentation
topics.summary: District administrators presented the preliminary FY28 operating budget of $27,514,571, representing a 5.36% or $1,399,853 increase over FY27. Primary cost drivers include salaries, a 41% rise in out-of-district special education tuitions, transportation increases of 13%, and utilities. The committee discussed scenarios for meeting town guidance, including a 3% target that requires $616,411 in reductions or a level-funded budget requiring $1.4 million in cuts and the elimination of approximately 15 staff positions.
key_details: The preliminary FY28 budget is $27,514,571, an increase of $1,399,853 (5.36%) for level service.
Salaries account for roughly 80% of the operational budget increase.
Non-public school special education tuition increased by 41% before state circuit breaker offsets.
Reaching the town's suggested 3% increase would require cutting $616,411, while a level-funded budget would require cutting $1.4 million and roughly 15 staff positions.
Administration warned that level-funding the budget would severely impact class sizes, academic programs, and student services.
topics.outcome: The superintendent will present a refined recommended budget in December after meeting with the Select Board on November 17.
topics.why_it_matters: A 5.36% increase will require town support and possibly an override; forcing the budget down to a level-funded limit would trigger 15 layoffs and reductions in school programming.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee distributed the approved policy on medication administration in schools (J-220), reviewed the personnel report showing one appointment and three resignations, approved warrants and payrolls, and approved meeting minutes from October 14, 2026.
key_details: Distributed updated school medication administration policy J-220.
Noted three resignations (one in SEDP, two education support professionals) and one appointment.
Approved open meeting and executive session minutes from October 14, 2026.

votes.motion: Accept the FY27 monthly general fund report as of October 31, 2026 and approve overexpended function codes.
Approve the FY27 federal and state grants in the amount of $747,857 as presented.

public_comment.summary: A resident commented on the MSBA decision, noting that a five-year delay with 4% annual construction cost inflation amounts to roughly a 22% cost escalation, meaning an MSBA reimbursement rate below that threshold would result in a net financial loss for the town even before accounting for educational impacts.
